title: Zero-point theorems in quantum many-body physics
abstract: We propose several zero-point type arguments based on the inevitable zero point(s) of a spectral gap in the quantum spin system phase diagrams in various dimensions. We consider multi-parameter families of Hamiltonian extending the conventional zero-point theorem that includes only one parameter. Analogously to the zero-point theorem, we only impose model-independent transformation relations along the parameter boundary, rather than specifying any low-energy dynamics or response. We further give a series of conjectures, which generalize our statements in a uniform way. Our results give powerful and universal model-independent constraints on the possible relevant operators for critical phenomena in quantum spin models in arbitrary high dimensions.
summary: This paper develops generalized zero-point theorems for quantum spin systems by analyzing the spectral gap function across multi-parameter families of Hamiltonians. By imposing only model-independent symmetry constraints on the parameter boundaries, the authors prove that the gap must close at certain points. This yields universal restrictions on the relevant operators governing critical behavior in high dimensions.
main_problem: To establish powerful, model-independent constraints on relevant operators governing critical phenomena in quantum spin models across arbitrary high dimensions.
main_result: The authors propose and generalize zero-point theorems showing that the spectral gap function must vanish at certain points within multi-parameter families of Hamiltonians under specific symmetry constraints.
method: The core method generalizes mathematical zero-point arguments by applying model-independent transformation relations (like those relating boundary conditions) to the gap function $\Delta(H)$ across continuous parameter spaces.
model_or_system: The study focuses on quantum many-body systems, specifically spin-1/2 models defined on lattices (chains and 2D square lattices), parameterized by multiple coupling constants or symmetries ($\mathbb{Z}_2 	imes \mathbb{Z}_2$, etc.).
key_observables: The spectral gap function $\Delta(H) = \lim_{L	o\infty} E_2(H) - E_1(H)$, which signals the presence or absence of a gap.
important_parameters: The dimensionality ($d$) and the number of continuous parameters ($p$) defining the Hamiltonian family, as well as symmetry constraints ($\mathbb{Z}_2$, $T$).
main_assumptions: The theorems only require imposing model-independent transformation data on the parameter boundary, avoiding assumptions about specific low-energy dynamics or response functions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the mathematical zero-point theorem and its quantum mechanical analogues, showing gap closing. They also visualize the geometric generalization of these theorems to two parameters in 2D lattices.
paper_structure: The paper builds from a basic one-parameter zero-point theorem (Theorem 0) to generalizations involving multiple parameters (Theorem 2), culminating in conjectures for $p$-parameter families on $d$-dimensional lattices.
why_interesting: This work provides universal, symmetry-based constraints on critical points that are independent of detailed low-energy Hamiltonians, offering a powerful theoretical tool applicable across various quantum phases studied in AMO and condensed matter physics.
